newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Kuchma accepts top reformer resignation.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Kuchma accepts top reformer resignation.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma accepted on Monday the resignation of Viktor Pynzenyk, deputy prime minister in charge of economic reform, a spokeswoman for Pynzenyk said.
"The president signed the deputy prime minister's resignation offer at the insistence of Viktor Mikhailovich (Pyzenyk)," Tamara Kutsai, the former minister's spokeswoman, told Reuters.
Kuchma's office could not immediately confirm that the president had approved Pynzenyk's resignation, tendered last Wednesday in anger over failure to pass this year's budget.

The president's press service said three days ago that Kuchma had ordered Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko to take a final decision about the offer by Pynzenyk, a leading reformer popular with Western funding bodies.

Kuchma at the weekend again blamed Lazarenko for the absence of a budget and a package of tax reforms to underpin it without which Ukraine cannot receive a multi-billion-dollar credit from the International Monetary Fund.
Pynzenyk has repeatedly criticised the government and parliament for dragging their heels in implementing stringent reform measures to pull Ukraine out of economic decline.
